name: Pulumi
description: Protects against destructive Pulumi operations like destroy \ and up with -y (auto-approve)

destructive_patterns.name: destroy
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi destroy removes ALL managed infrastructure. Use 'pulumi preview --diff' first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi destroy removes ALL managed infrastructure:

\ - Every resource in your stack is destroyed \ - Cloud resources (VMs, databases, networks) deleted \ - Cannot be undone without backups/recreation \ - Use --target to destroy specific resources only

\ Preview first: pulumi preview --diff

destructive_patterns.name: up-yes
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi up -y skips confirmation. Remove -y flag for safety.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi up -y skips confirmation:

\ - No opportunity to review changes before applying \ - Intended for CI/CD, not interactive use \ - Changes may destroy or recreate resources \ - Replacements can cause downtime

\ For safety: remove -y and review the preview

destructive_patterns.name: state-delete
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi state delete removes resource from state without destroying it.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi state delete orphans resources:

\ - Resource removed from Pulumi state \ - Actual cloud resource still exists \ - Resource becomes 'unmanaged' (Pulumi ignores it) \ - May cause drift between state and reality

\ Consider: pulumi refresh to sync state with reality

destructive_patterns.name: stack-rm
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi stack rm removes the stack. Use --force only if stack is empty.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi stack rm removes the entire stack:

\ - Stack and its state deleted \ - Does NOT destroy actual infrastructure (unless empty) \ - --force required if resources still exist \ - Resources become unmanaged (orphaned)

\ Destroy resources first: pulumi destroy, then rm stack

destructive_patterns.name: refresh-yes
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi refresh -y auto-approves state changes. Review changes first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi refresh -y auto-approves state sync:

\ - Syncs Pulumi state with actual cloud resources \ - May delete resources from state if not found \ - May update state with drift from cloud

\ Run without -y first to review detected changes

destructive_patterns.name: cancel
destructive_patterns.description: pulumi cancel terminates an in-progress update, which may leave resources in inconsistent state.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
pulumi cancel stops in-progress operations:

\ - Terminates currently running update/destroy \ - Resources may be left in inconsistent state \ - Some resources created, others not \ - May require manual cleanup

\ Use only when operation is stuck/hung
